description:
Design decision (2026-08-15): materializers do not hold the WAL back and do not talk to the log in the data plane. A materializer's life: load latest snapshot at S -> ShardServer.pull from S+1 (chunks for old ranges, buffer for recent — continuous by construction since buffered entries stay pullable until their chunk write confirms) -> stay live. No catch-up mode vs live mode distinction; the floor-exceeded special case dissolves into the normal path. The WAL trim floor becomes purely object-storage confirmation.

Required plumbing:
1. Version currency: shard-server pull replies / long-poll wakeups carry a high-water version ('no data for you, but you are current through v') — FDB's empty-tag peek shape. Demux sees every version at commit granularity; pull-driven, no per-commit fan-out.
2. The stream also carries the known-committed version (KCV, from the epic's durability invariant); olivine applies everything immediately for read currency but gates window eviction/persistence at KCV, so recovery rollback to RV (always >= KCV-at-crash, since every log receives every version) is pure in-memory pointer discard — never disk surgery.
3. Discovery: materializer finds its ShardServer via director/TSL (or the existing log get_shard_server introduction); no other log contact. Recovery coordination stays director-mediated.
4. Multi-shard materializers merge N shard streams by version (aligns materializer scope with the shard, as the per-shard snapshot handle already assumes).
5. Retire: olivine's Log.pull path, the interim chunk catch-up special case, and basalt's subscriber usage (decide basalt's fate: port to demux streaming or deprecate — review finding 5).
6. Fix in passing: interim catch-up runs synchronously in the olivine server and floods its own mailbox (review finding 9) — the streaming rewrite replaces it with a backpressured task like normal pulling.

Pre-quorum exposure note: streaming from the buffer has the same exposure as Log.pull today (demux receives pushes at WAL-append time, before quorum ack); the KCV eviction gate plus rollback-at-unlock is the answer in both worlds, and no client ever observes the uncommitted suffix because read versions are KCV by construction.
title: Materializers stream from the Demux; the log's only consumer is its Demux
